Hill Mari is characterized by vowel harmony (syngharmonism), which is particularly well developed in the mountain dialect. Both vowels and consonants are subject to this harmony. Mari is the titular and official language of its republic, alongside Russian. The Mari language today has three standard forms: Hill Mari, Northwestern Mari, and Meadow Mari. Hill Mari, the second literary standard of Mari, is used by less than 10% of Mari native speakers, but is nonetheless the working language of a vibrant culture and literature that has to date been largely inaccessible to outsiders due to a dearth of teaching and reference materials. Hill Mari, also referred to as Western Mari, forms one of the primary literary standards within the Mari language group, distinct from Meadow Mari (the basis for the dominant standard) and Eastern Mari.
